item.title: Hours after U.S. imposes tariffs, Canada says it'll strike back starting Sept. 8
item.description: The U.S. has now imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products. Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada will match those tariffs "dollar for dollar" next month.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. has now imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products. Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada will match those tariffs "dollar for dollar" next month.

(Image credit: Graham Hughes)

item.title: Big tech companies will have to pay to publish Australian news content under new laws
item.description: Australia has passed a law requiring major tech platforms such as Google and Meta to strike deals with Australian news publishers or pay a levy on their advertising revenue.
item.content:encoded: Australia has passed a law requiring major tech platforms such as Google and Meta to strike deals with Australian news publishers or pay a levy on their advertising revenue.
item.dc:creator: Kristina Kukolja

item.title: Top Iran official says U.S. focus on economic warfare shows it has failed militarily
item.description: The Iranian regime has dismissed President Trump's threats to crush Iran economically, saying that years of U.S. sanctions have failed.

item.title: Trump declares economic warfare on Iran. And, SCOTUS to rule on White House ballroom

item.title: U.S. debt tops $40 trillion. And, new census report Trump is touting raises concerns
item.description: The U.S. debt has surpassed $40 trillion. And, a new census report on noncitizen voting that President Trump is touting has ties to a think tank aligned with him, raising concerns among experts.

item.title: North Korea fires a suspected missile toward the sea, Japan says
item.description: The suspected launch on Thursday comes a day after North Korea shrugged off a U.S. decision to scale back military drills with South Korea in an apparent bid to resume diplomacy.

item.title: Chinese court sentences founder of property developer Evergrande to life in prison
item.description: Chinese property developer Hui Ka Yan has been sentenced to life in prison. The decision marks a milestone in Evergrande's saga after it collapsed with more than $300 billion in liabilities.
